What do you think makes a bad parent? A good one?

A good one = love, patience and understanding.

A bad one = none of the above.

A bad parent is one who thinks that they are always right on everything, how to do something, what to do, and how to think. And if a person does not bend to those demands there are consequences.

A good parent gently guides a child into their own beliefs but protects them from the worst of life.

Heaps of things, I'm sure many people will list good ones. So I'll just list one that I think is important, along with many others.

Preparing your child for the real goddamned world.

Sure, you can coddle them until they graduate college where they find out very quickly how terrible the world can be. Or you can grow a resilient, independent person with worth to society. So many kids I've seen go through college taking on debt because they've never had a job, never had to budget, never known what people really do expect of them. They barely read books/news/anything longer than a twitter post... I know I'm describing a very vague person here that we all seem to hate, but they're more common than you think.

Raise a person, not a child.

I strive to be a good parent. When my daughters are fighting, I will calm them down and try to understand what is the cause of the problem. My wife will simply yell at them and spank them, which of course teaches them nothing.

For teaching perspective:

Bad parent teaches "this is how things are."

Good parent teaches "this is what we've learned so far."

I know parents that shower their kids with expensive gifts but it's not what counts. My children love me and tell me constantly. I am quite happy to share my secret with any other parent out there. Its very simple

Spend time with your kids!

Its that easy. When I am not working I spend time with them. I read to them, I listen to them, I encourage them. On the weekends I wake early and take them out for walks. When I go out somewhere boring like shopping or the DIY store I ask if they would like to come with me. They nearly always say yes. They would rather be with me somewhere boring than not spend time with me. Have time for your kids and the rewards are amazing.

When disciplining a child they have to have a clear reason as to why what they did was wrong and if possible explain the ramifications of their actions are. A simple "because I said so" won't inspire a sense of right and wrong in a child, only enforcing a sense that if you're not around to discipline them then they are free to do what they want.

Never stop answering the "why" questions, any question asked by a child should be answered because it's a genuine interest in learning being displayed, and no-one should ever stifle that.

A child should never fear their parents, beating them and yelling is a sure-fire way to make a child not come to you if they're scared and they think they've done something wrong.

Don't stop your child from going out or socializing just because you want to protect them from the outside world, it's just going to leave them emotionally stunted and more vulnerable than before. Though if what they're doing is actively dangerous make sure they know that.

Spend time with your kids, one of the best things about growing up was going fishing with my dad, time spent with children allows them to learn from you and will form memories that they'll cherish for the rest of their lives.

Try and see things from the perspective of your child, do they look up to you? Do they understand what you're trying to say? Do they know that you're going to be patient with them.

I think a parents job is to prepare children for the world. A good parents balances introducing them to responsibility and skills that they need to learn but doesn't overwhelm them too much. So a bad parent is one that encourages children to never become independent and doesn't give them the skills they need or goes too far the other way and acts like a drill sergeant and leaves them traumatised.

What a loaded question. Ignoring things like being abusive or manipulative (others will probably cover this). A good parent teaches their children how to think instead of just loading them up with their opinions and facts, so they grow up able to think, evaluate and understand things critically. A good parent teaches by example; children are like sponges soaking in memories and influences even if they don't understand them yet. Don't say "always be honest" and then just pocket the extra change you got.

A good parent talks to their child instead of always using the classic "because I said so" (this fosters resentment and rebellion later). When i was growing up my dad always tried to explain things to me logically eg, "Do you understand why you shouldn't do that thing? No? Ok because A. B. C and D. " Then if I did that thing anyway I'd get in trouble and know I'd deserved it.

Another really important one is respect. Teach children to respect others and to respect themselves. Don't patronize. Kids can pick up on this and push back. My dad always spoke to me like an adult, explained things and it was ok to not always agree. I always felt lucky to have that and its a big part of who i am. Basically just because its a kid doesn't mean they ( and their ideas etc) shouldn't be respected.

This is just stuff based on my own experience and life, also i guess this only really applies to prepubescent and above ages.

My version of the answers, FWIW:

Good parents: Do all they can to educate, prepare and shape their kids by understanding them and giving quality time and experiences. Discipline should be fair and appropriate for the infraction. Explanations of why they are being punished should always be given in a manner that the children will understand. Letting kids be themselves is important, even if it goes against what your beliefs are. Guide them but don't force you will if it is not a critical life lesson or mistake in the making. When injured or sick, do all you can to remedy the situation instead of merely "caring" for the child. Give quality time rather than just quantity. Love unconditionally and forgive generously. Above all, listen before making judgement and show compassion, fairness and interest.

Bad parents: Will control every aspect of the child's life. They will not allow individuality outside of the "proper" behavior defined by the parent's own desires. Not listening to kids or shouting over them will only serve to drive a wedge between the child and parent. Ignoring a child's age when deciding a punishment or seriousness of a rule infraction will not teach a kid anything and serve only to fuel disdain. Living vicariously through your children prevents them from becoming their own person and shows the selfishness of the parent. Doing things that make you feel better instead of the child when bad things happen is psychologically harmful. Using a child as a pawn in a game of control is despicable and shows the weakness of a bad parent. Lying to a child for convenience is not something that should become a parenting style.

Being fickle with permission. Kids are pretty well aware of the distinction between consistant rules and arbotrary denials. I had a group of about 5 friends growing up. 2 of them had parents who would keep their kids home for a weekend for petty reasons. After 18 those kids were the first to get tatoos, try harder drugs, and get in trouble with the law.

A good parent is actively engaged in making their child into a fully functional adult. A bad parent is one who is one who is preventing them from that, or just unwilling to put forth any effort to achieve that goal.
I don't have kids, so I'd say I'm a pretty good parent.
